title: Finite projection exchange transposes
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. Use the small pro-etale coefficient categories and the specified six operations of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Finite inputs used for compact support carry compatible etale-origin witnesses; integral inputs are derived complete with compatible witnessed finite reductions, rational operations are raw localization, and algebraically closed coefficients are represented at a common finite coefficient field. All operations below are restricted to their stated constructible domains; tensor factors and comparisons have their stated finite-Tor hypotheses. Fix $n\ge1$ and $\Lambda=A_n$. Let $(f',g',f,g)$ be a Cartesian square of separated finite-type morphisms of finite-type $k$-schemes, with $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\to X$; the schemes $X,Y,Y'$ need not be separated over $k$. For $K\in D^b_c(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, use the counit-defined projection $\operatorname{PF}$ and compact-support exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ of [def-exchange-projection], formed for a compactification $f=pj$ and its base change. When $X,Y,Y'$ are separated over $k$, setting (i) of [lem-sp-compact-projection-base-change] with $A=\Lambda$ gives, for one fixed compactification and with canonical tensor/pullback comparisons inserted,
$$\operatorname{Ex}_{!,K\otimes^L Lf^*L}\circ Lg^*\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}=\operatorname{PF}_{f',Lg'^*K,Lg^*L}\circ(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,K}\otimes1).$$
The present statement asserts in addition the following.
(1) The displayed equation holds for every compactification $f=pj$ also when $X,Y,Y'$ are only of finite type over $k$. More precisely, base change the compactification, write $h:\bar X'\to\bar X$, and $M=j_!K$. The open-factor routes have source and target in the essential image of $j'_!$ and, under the canonical open units, both restrictions equal the identity of $Lg'^*K\otimes^L Lf'^*Lg^*L$. For the proper factor, both maps from $Lg^*(Rp_*M\otimes^L L)$ to $Rp'_*(Lh^*M\otimes^L Lp'^*Lg^*L)$ have the same $Lp'^*\dashv Rp'_*$ transpose
$$Lp'^*Lg^*(Rp_*M\otimes^L L)\cong Lh^*Lp^*Rp_*M\otimes^L Lp'^*Lg^*L\xrightarrow{Lh^*\varepsilon_{p,M}\otimes1}Lh^*M\otimes^L Lp'^*Lg^*L.$$
These identifications use the canonical ringed tensor/square comparison, rather than an arbitrary tensor structure.
(2) For two compactifications related by a refinement, the compactification-comparison isomorphisms of [def-fix-six-functor-datum] intertwine the two equations of (1); hence the equation holds for the compactification-independent maps $\operatorname{PF}$ and $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ of [def-fix-six-functor-datum].
(3) For $f=\mathrm{id}$ with the identity compactification, the projection map is the identity under the unit identifications.

proof.text: Use tensor_square for the specified fixed-scalar monoidal square. For the route that exchanges first, tensor naturality and mateEquiv_counit compute its transpose explicitly as commonTranspose. For the route that projects first, move the projection past theta by naturality, use the projection counit equation, then tensor naturality and tensor_square to obtain the same commonTranspose. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom equivalence gives equality of the proper routes.

Apply open_factor_assembly to that proper-route equality. This gives the diamond and both open restriction equations. An explicit composite of mu, tensor of beta with identity, and gamma identifies the open source with an extension-by-zero object; the target is already an extension-by-zero object. These are the two essential-image assertions.

Use refinement_left for the left word. Rewrite both right words by the diamond equality to obtain refinement intertwining for the right word. This proves RefinementLaw without repeating the domain or comparison calculations.

Specialize identity_normalization to the fixed scalar positive-level coefficient ring and X. Assemble the eight clauses of SquareLaw and the identity clause of FiniteStatement, preserving every original hypothesis.
